Eve — quick technical guidance below. I copied the short bits you can paste into procurement.

1) Baseline SLOs (public Hosted API, standard model tier):
   - p50: 120 ms (in-region token latency)
   - p95: 420 ms (in-region token latency)

2) Measurement semantics:
   - Measurement unit: per-request token generation latency (end-to-end server-side), aggregated by region/POP.
   - Windowing: rolling 30-day window for continuous measurement; monthly reporting windows available on request.
   - Exclusions: Planned maintenance windows (with >=72h notice) and force majeure events are excluded. Also excluded are customer-driven traffic patterns outside standard usage (e.g., sustained unbounded sequence lengths or non-standard quantized models).

3) Conditional enterprise commitments (we often offer these under Dedicated/Private or with contract addendum):
   - Pin to specific model version (e.g., gpt-3.8-redwood-v1) and max sequence length (e.g., 4k tokens).
   - Provide a P50/P95 SLA for a 24-hour rolling window for high-tier customers as a paid upgrade.

Suggested short clause for procurement (copy/paste):
"Redwood Inference commits to best-effort Hosted API latency targets of p50 = 120 ms and p95 = 420 ms per-region for standard text-generation endpoints, measured on a per-request token latency basis using a rolling 30-day window. These commitments apply to traffic within normal usage profiles as defined in Appendix A (model pinned, maximum sequence length 4,096 tokens). Planned maintenance, force majeure, and customer-initiated non-standard traffic are excluded from measurement. Commercial SLAs with tighter windows or fixed uptime targets are available under Redwood Dedicated or via an addendum to this agreement."

If procurement pushes for fixed p95 targets with penalties, loop Legal and Sales Ops — we usually avoid hard financial penalties on Hosted unless it's a committed dedicated plan.

-ben
Ben Carter
Head of Serving & Runtime, Redwood Inference
